Ten comments

The Ornithologist

I heard this recently played at a session by a local concertinist, and made up an accompanying part to it - as shown. It was composed by Freeland Barbour of Orkney. It’s an example of what I call a ‘fairground’ tune - one that sounds quite lively and that you could imagine being played on a merry-go-round steam organ. It was referred to in a discussion thread where it was reported that it didn’t show up on this site, so here it is.

It wraps round to end on an A part, when the 1st- and 2nd-time bars should be ignored and the coda bar played.
If listening to it on the auto-play, set the speed to about 50% of the default tempo.

↳ Posted by Bazza on March 29th, 2025.

Re: The Ornithologist

Thanks Michael. I couldn’t see how to edit the headers on the ABC version when posting the piece, so couldn’t change the L: number: how did you do that?

I place chords between the staves because I used to play with an accordionist who took the lower harmonies. It was easier if he could avoid darting his eyes around the page to see both the bottom line and the chords simultaneously, especially when sight reading at speed.

↳ Posted by Bazza on March 30th, 2025.

Re: The Ornithologist

Freeland, Orkney… ? Don’t think so.

↳ Posted by Kenny on March 30th, 2025.

Re: The Ornithologist

Indeed not.

From Perthshire near Pitlochry originally but well travelled in person and musically.
He’s keenly interested in Scandinavian music inc Orkney, Shetland(near enough).

I have his two volumes “Music and The Land”. Lots of great music from “all over” with beautiful pictures and good stories too.

↳ Posted by 🎻 Melody Player 🎻 on March 30th, 2025.

Re: The Ornithologist

Some accounts suggest he was born in Edinburgh although his own website doesn’t mention this.
However he spent most of his early years between Edinburgh and Glen Fincastle near Pitlochry.
